title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Does extract_deposit_data always return exactly 192 bytes on successful execution?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Analysis of deposit data extraction in Prysm reveals that the specification-level function 'extract_deposit_data' does not have a direct Go implementation. Instead, Prysm uses ABI unpacking via the Ethereum deposit contract interface. The actual implementation is in UnpackDepositLogData() which extracts 5 variable-length byte slices from the DepositEvent log data. These slices are then assembled into a Deposit_Data structure. The total output size is NOT guaranteed to be exactly 192 bytes by the extraction logic itself - instead, size validation occurs implicitly through the ABI unpacking and subsequent data structure constraints.

go_implementations.description: Unpacks DepositEvent log data using Ethereum ABI decoder to extract 5 byte slices: pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount, signature, index
Processes unpacked deposit log data and constructs ethpb.Deposit_Data structure

state_anomalies_found.description: The function returns 5 byte slices with no explicit length validation at extraction time

recommendations.proposed_fix:

  - len(pubkey) == 48
  - len(withdrawalCredentials) == 32
  - len(amount) == 8
  - len(signature) == 96
  - len(index) == 8
Return error if any size check fails
